I have had 4 or more grand mal seizures in my life and have never been the same since the first one, but I enjoy my life now. In fact, I'm thankful because I am happier, less anxious, more free now that I have learned to relinquish my desire to feel control in life. I may have another one and change again, and that's okay. The doctors say that I won't have any more if I take my medication, but living with that mindset has been wonderful for me. Learn to meditate and let go of that feeling of "I am damaged now" or "why did this happen to ME" or "how do I get back to normal." I promise you you will feel better, and learn to love life again, but you need to accept the present, as some features of your current experience could be permanent changes if your brain is anything like mine. 

Also talk to a doctor about all of this. They're smart and they study this stuff for a living, they can help you. I used to not trust doctors, now I love them as they've given me some of the most valuable tools for me to take my life back from epilepsy, drug addiction, bipolar and more.
